And they abode at Chatzerot is connected to And…Miriam spoke (12:1), for they abode there on her account. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.
And Miriam…spoke. Miriam spoke. Aharon agreed or was silent.

Now va-tedabber is in the feminine. Thus our verse is to be rendered, And Miriam spoke, and Aharon. If both spoke, then our text should have read, va-yedabberu miriam ve-aharon. Hence he was also punished.Va-tedabber (spoke) is followed by a bet and has a negative connotation. It is similar to va-yedabber ha-am be-Elokim (And the people spoke against Elokim) (Bamidbar 21:5). The verb dabber (spoke) followed by a bet is also found with a positive connotation. It also appears in prophetic statements. Some say that Moshe was king of Kush and took a Kushi woman. Onkelos renders Kushi, beautiful. According to Onkelos, Kushi is an honorific term. The Arvim similarly call pitch white. We too refer to a blind person by the term sege nahor (rich of light). But it is illogical to turn a positive name into a negative one. Some say that Kush the Binyamini (Tehillim 7:1) refers to Shaul. They say the same with regard to Are ye not as the children of the Ethiopians (Khushiyyim) unto Me (Amos 9:7). I have already explained this.I believe that the Kushi woman is to be identified with Tzipporah, for Tzipporah was a Midyani. The Midyanim are Yishmeelim and they live in tents. Scripture similarly writes: The curtains of the land of Midyan do tremble (Chavakuk 3:7). Because of the sun they do not have any whiteness at all. Tzipporah was black and was like a Kushi.

[For he had married a Kushi woman.] These are the words that Miriam spoke. How precious are the words of the ancients who said with regard to the elders, “Happy are they, but woe to their wives.” They suspected that Moshe refrained from sleeping with Tzipporah only because she was not beautiful.

And they said: hath Hashem indeed spoken only with Moshe? Miriam offered proof that Moshe did not act in this manner because of the sanctity of Hashem, for they too were prophets and they were not prohibited from engaging in sexual intercourse.

Only with. Scripture reads, ha-rak akh. One term would have sufficed. However, Scripture is employing elegant language. Compare, ha-mi-mi-beli en kevarim (because there were no graves) (Shemot 14:11).
And Hashem heard it. Even though they spoke in secret.
Was very meek. The word anav (meek) is similar to the word shalev (at peace) (Iyov 16:12). Its meaning is that Moshe did not seek honor over his brother.

Suddenly. The mem of pitom (suddenly) is superfluous. It is like the mem of shilshom (three days ago). Pitom is related to peti (a thoughtless one) (Mishlei 9:4). It refers to something that one did not think of.

Come out ye three unto the Tent of Meeting. Each one from his tent. Scripture first speaks generally. It then goes into detail, namely, And Hashem came down in a pillar of cloud…and called Aharon and Miriam (v. 5), and Moshe heard.
Hear now my words. The word na means now.
A prophet among you. If there be a prophet of Hashem among you.

In a vision The meaning of im yiheyeh nevi’akhem Adonai (if there be a prophet among you, I Hashem) is, if there be a prophet, one who is a prophet of Elokim among you. Compare, ve-hanevu’ah oded ha-navi (even the prophecy of Oded the prophet (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8); and ha-ohelah sarah immo (his mother Sarah’s tent) (Bereshit 24:67); and kisakha Elokim olam (Thy throne given of Elokim is for ever) (Tehillim 45:7).
In a vision. In the visions of the night.
I do speak with him in a dream. Scripture repeats itself as is its style in prophecies.

He is trusted in all my house. It means that Moshe is, at it were, a member of My house. He enters without permission. If necessary he states his needs. However, in your case when I make myself known to you in a dream, then you are informed. If not, then you have no permission to ask.
With him do I speak mouth to mouth. The meaning is, I speak to him without an intermediary.
Even manifestly, and not in dark speeches. This means I illustrate my word to him as I did when I commanded the erection of the tabernacle.
And not in dark speeches. Compare, A great eagle (…Came unto Levanon, And took the top of the cedar) (Yechezkel 17:3).
And the similitude of Hashem doth he behold. As in the case of Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory (Shemot 33:18). Or its meaning is that Hashem communicates with Moshe when Moshe is awake.
And he departed. The reference is to God’s glory. And when the cloud was removed (v. 10) proves this.
From over the tent. From over the opening of the tent.
And…behold, Miriam was leprous. Ve-hinneh metzora’at is to be rendered, and behold, “she” [Miriam] was leprous. Compare, ka’asher ka’ah (as it vomited out) (Vayikra 18:28).
Oh my Lord. I have already explained the meaning of bi adoni (Oh my lord).
Lay not, I pray thee. The meaning of al na (…not, I pray thee) is, now, do not.

We have done foolishly. The word no’alnu (we have done foolishly) is a nifal. It has no cognate except for the word no’alu (are become fools) in The princes of Tzoan are become fools (Is. 19:13). Some say that the root of no’alnu was formed by inverting the root ivvelet (foolishness). Compare, Foolishness is bound up (Mishlei 22:15) (in the heart of a child). The meaning of no’alnu is known.

Let her not, I pray, be as one dead. Let our sister not now be as a stillborn child, half of whose flesh is consumed when it comes out of its mother’s womb. The same is true of the flesh of a leper. There is no need for a scribal emendation.
And Moshe cried. This shows that Moshe was pained because of what happened to his sister.

O Hashem. You who hold the power in Your hands, heal her now. Hashem therefore answered him as follows: If her father was angry at her and spat in her face, would she not hide in shame from seeing his face for seven days?
Shut up. As lepers are, so that they do not harm others.

And after that she shall be brought in again. Ve-acher te’asef (and after that she shall be brought in again) means she shall once again be considered as a member of the community. Va-asafto (and you shall bring him in) in and you shall bring him in from his leprosy (Melachim II 5:3) is similar. After Miriam returned to the camp, the people journeyed from Chatzerot.

And pitched in the wilderness of Paran. Many believe that the cloud was there. They interpret thus because they found Scripture stating and the cloud abode in the wilderness of Paran (Bamidbar 10:12). They interpret And when the cloud was removed from over the Tent (v. 10) literally. However, I believe that this is not the correct meaning.
Send thou men. Scripture records that Hashem told Yisrael: go up, take possession (Devarim 1:21) and Yisrael answered: Let us send men before us (Devarim 1:22). Hashem then said, Send thou men.
The meaning of men is, men known for their might. The same applies to all of them men (v. 3) and to be thou [Shlomo] strong and show thyself a man (Melachim I 2:2), for he [Shlomo] was a man.
That they may spy out. The meaning of ve-yaturu (that they may spy out) is that they may search out. Compare, ve-lo taturu (and that ye go not about) (Bamidbar 15:39).

Every one a prince among them. Kol nasi ba-hem is to be interpreted: each one was a prince among them. On the other hand, the word ehad mentioned earlier in our verse also applies here. Compare, And two men, captains of bands, were [captains of] the son of Shaul (Shmuel II 4:2). There are many such examples.

[These are the names of the men.] The reason that Scripture states, these are the names of the men, after earlier stating, And these were their names (v. 4), is to teach us that, unlike Hoshea, their names were never changed.

Get you up here into the south. Get you up this way in the south. It is known that Mitzrayim is south of the land of Yisrael, as I have explained in the Book of Daniel. The following is proof of this. Mitzrayim is less than thirty degrees north of the equator. Yerushalayim is thirty-three degrees north of the equator. The desert of Paran is south of the land of Kenaan. Observe that the meaning of in the South is not south of the camp but in the south of the land of Kenaan. Proof of the aforementioned is that Scripture tells us concerning Chevron, which belonged to the tribe of Yehudah, Yehudah shall abide in his border on the south (Yehoshua 18:5).
And see the land, what it is. And the people, what is it?
Whether they are strong. In battle. Scripture then goes on to explain, and see the land. It says, and what the land is…whether it is good, that is, whether its air and water are good.
Whether in camps. Like the Kederites, who live in tents.
Whether it is fat. In producing wheat.
[And came unto Chevron.] Our sages of blessed memory said that and came refers to Kalev the son of Yefuneh, for each one of the men went to a different part of the country.

Tzoan in Mitzrayim. Tzoan is the name of a city in Mitzrayim. Of Beth-lehem Yehudah (Rut 1:1) is similar. Some say that the word tzo’an (Tzoan) is connected to the word yitzan (be removed) in A tent that shall not be removed (Is. 33:20). However, this is farfetched.
Scripture mentions Chevron in order to tell us that Chevron came into being before Tzoan.
Unto the valley of eshcol. These are the words of Moshe. It is possible that it is similar to and pursued as far as Dan (Bereshit 14:14) in that it had another name.
Was called. Kara (was called) is to be rendered, someone called. Compare, whom she bore to Levi (Bamidbar 26:59).

[At the end.] The word mi-ketz (at the end) sometimes means at the beginning and sometimes means at the end. Mi-ketz arba’im yom (and the end of forty days) probably means at the start of the fortieth day.
And they went. This informs us that they did not go to their tents, which were in the camp, but immediately went [to Moshe, Aharon, and all the congregation].
And brought back word. To Moshe and Aharon.
And they told him. They told Moshe, for he was the most important one.
And Kalev stilled the people. Rabbi Yonah the grammarian says that the meaning of va-yahas (and…stilled) is: and he said be still (hasu).

And they spread an evil report of the land. Va-yotzi’u dibbat ha-aretz (and they spread an evil report) means: and they spread a lie. This is not the meaning of va-yave yosef et dibbatam ra (and Yosef brought evil report of them) (Bereshit 37:2), for va-yave (brought) is the reverse of va-yotzi (and they spread).

Evil report. The word dibbah (evil report) comes from a double root. It comes from the same root as the word dovev (moving gently) in Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep (Cant. 7:10). I have explained it in its place.
Eateth up the inhabitants thereof. For its air is bad.

Men of great stature. Every man is a man of measurements. Anshe middot means men of great measurement, men whose measurements are greater than everyone else’s. The same applies to the phrase anshe levav (men of heart) (Iyov. 34:34). There are many other instances similar to the above.
The nephilim. I have already explained this term.
Of the nephilim. Its meaning is that they were of the Nefilim, who were in the earth in those days, and also after that when…came in (Bereshit 6:4). I have explained it there.
Their voice. Et kolam (their voice) is the object of va-tissa (lifted up) and also of va-yittenu (and cried).
Murmured. Va-yillonu (murmured) is a nifal. It is an ayin vav. When conjugated in the nifal it looks like a whole root.

To return into Mitzrayim. Shuv (to return) is an infinitive. It is like the word kum (to stand) in I am not able to stand (Eichah 1:14) and kum (rising up) in And the king, against whom there is no rising up (Mishlei 30:31).
Then Moshe…fell. By his own will.
And Yehoshua the son of nun. Moshe mentions Yehoshua first out of regard for Yehoshua’s elevated status.
For they are bread. We will eat them like bread. Who eat up My people as they eat bread (Tehillim 14:4) is similar.
Their defense is removed from over them. For the heart of a warrior frets when he does not have a shield to protect him and to serve as a shade for him.
Bade stone them. Yehoshua and Kalev.
Despise me. Yena’atzuni (despise me) means anger me. It has many cognates in Scripture.
Scripture employs the singular be-kirbo (among them) because at first they were united to do good.

When the Mitzrim shall hear–for thou broughtest up this people. The meaning of ki he’elita (for thou broughtest up) is: that you brought up. After Scripture states, When the Mitzrim shall hear (ve-shame’u)…they will say to the inhabitants of this land, the reference being to the land of Kenaan, it goes on to explain what the Mitzrim heard. Scripture therefore repeats the word shame’u (have heard) and states they have heard (shame’u) that Thou Hashem [Thy glory] art in the midst of this people (v. 14).

Art seen face to face. The reference is to the glory which the elders saw (Shemot 24:9,10), or to the appearance of the glory of Hashem…in the eyes of the children of Yisrael (Shemot 24:17). The latter is correct.

Art seen. The word nirah (seen) is a verb in the perfect. The meaning of attah Adonai nirah is, Thou Hashem were seen. Ve-nishar ani (and I was left) (Yechezkel 9: 8) is similar. So is ki umlal ani (for I languish away) (Tehillim 6:3), because the lamed of umlal is vocalized with a pattach.
Standeth over them. When they camp.
Then the nations which have heard the fame of thee. The reference is to Mitzrayim. Also to the Kenaani and other nations.

Able. The word yekholet (able) is a noun. It is similar to the word yevoshet (dried up) in until the waters were dried up (Bereshit 8:7). It does not mean a measure as in the midrashic interpretation.
Therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness. The meaning of va-yishchatem is, He hath slain them. Scripture employs the term va-yishchatem because sheep graze in the wilderness.

Let the power of the Lord be great. Let the power…be great connotes being slow to anger, for all who are long-suffering have the great power to break their anger. As Thou hast spoken, that you are slow to anger is proof of this. I have explained these attributes in the Torah portion Ki Tissa.

Pardon, I pray thee. Since we find Scripture saying surely they shall not see the land (v. 23) after salachti ke-devarekha (I have pardoned according to thy word) (v. 20), we learn that the term salach (pardon) refers to being slow to anger. Similarly, the meaning of ve-nislach lo (and he shall be forgiven) (Bamidbar 15:28) is [the punishment shall be held in abeyance] until he fully repents.
According unto the greatness of thy lovingkindness. The meaning of ke-godel chasdekha (according to the greatness of Thy lovingkindness) is: because of Thy great lovingkindness.
And according as thou hast forgiven. The word nasata (Thou hast forgiven) is similar to the word nose (forgiving) in forgiving sin (Shemot 34:7).

Even until now. Until this place or from the day that they left Mitzrayim until this very day, for the word hennah (now) can refer to a place or to a specific time. Compare, there came men in hither (hennah) (Yehoshua 2:2) and, and I have not seen him until now (hennah) (Bereshit 44:28). I have already explained this term.
As I live. It means as I live, so shall My word come to pass.
Shall be filled with the glory. As My glory fills the earth. However, it most probably refers to the future. Its meaning is, I shall do this so that my glory shall be known in the world.

These ten times. The meaning is, these many times. Scripture mentions ten because it is most important. It is the end of the one numbers and the first of the ten numbers in the second series of numbers.
Any of them that despised me. From among their children.

But my servant Kalev. Kalev alone is mentioned because he stilled the people (Bamidbar 13:30). The Leviyim and the kohanim are not included in the oath, for no prince from among them went to spy out the land. Furthermore, Scripture states, all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number (v. 29). Now even though there were no kohanim there, there were in reality many Leviyim there.
Another spirit. In contrast to the spies.
And hath followed me fully. He did not he but pursued my word and confirmed it by saying that the land is very good.

Now the Amaleki and the Kenaani. The Kenaani refers to the Emori, for every Emori is a Kenaani. Scripture does not bother to mention the Emori by name because the other nation mentioned is the Amaleki, who is of the children of Shem. On the other hand, Kenaan, who is the father of the Emori, is of the children of Cham. Then the Amaleki and the Kenaani…came down (Bamidbar 14:45) is similar. And the Emori…came out (Devarim 1:44) is proof of this. Scripture does not mention the Amaleki in the aforementioned verse, as the Emori was the more important.

Dwelt in the vale. To ambush you. Others say that the meaning of our verse is, even though the Amaleki and the Kenaani dwell in the valley, turn toward the way of the Red Sea and do not fear. Now Bnei Yisrael did not repent, hence Hashem’s word.
Your carcasses. The meaning of pigrekhem is your dead bodies.
Have murmured. Halinotem (have murmured) is related to the word va-yallinu (murmured) in and…murmured against Moshe (v. 2).
Concerning which I lifted up my hand. Scripture speaks as humans do, for the sky is above.
Kalev is mentioned first because he acted before anyone else to quiet the people.
Your carcasses. Namely, you.
Shall be wanderers. For it is the way of shepherds not to remain and rest in one place. My habitation is plucked up and carried away from me As a shepherd’s tent (Is. 38:12) is proof of this.
Your strayings. For you turned away from me and said, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Mitzrayim (Bamidbar 14:4).
Which ye spied out. By command.
My displeasure. I will break my word. Or, it means who shall break Me; that is, who shall break My oath. Compare, But if her father break (heni) her (Bamidbar 30:6).
That are gathered together against me. For they wanted to stone the servants of Hashem because they spoke of Hashem’s glory.
In this wilderness. The time set for each one shall come to an end, for God has set a specific time for everyone’s death.
And there they shall die. All of them, close to the time set by God.
And…MADE ALL THE CONGREGATION TO MURMUR AGAINST HIM. Va-yillonu (and made to murmur) is a hifil.
Died. Va-yamutu (died) is to interpreted as if written metu (died).
By the plague. All together.
But Yehoshua the son of nun. These are the words of Moshe. He mentions Yehoshua before Kalev.
Seeing it shall not prosper. The ascent of the mountain will not prosper. Or, the violation of Hashem’s command cannot prosper.
Forasmuch as ye are turned back. Ki al ken shavtem (forasmuch as ye are turned back) means, since you turned back. Compare, since (ki al ken) I gave her not (Bereshit 38:26).
But they presumed to go up. Va-yapilu (but they presumed) is related to the word ofel (mound) in the mound and the tower (Is. 32:14). The meaning of va-yapilu is, they went up the hill.

And beat them down. Rabbi Moshe the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that our text should have read va-yakkitum (and beat them down). Va-yadbeku (followed hard) in even they also followed hard after them (Shmuel I 14:22) is similar. However, I believe that va-yakketum (and beat them down) comes from a double root and is an irregular word.
Even unto Chormah. Chormah is the name of a place. Others say that the meaning of even unto Chormah is, until they destroyed them.

When ye are come into the land of your habitations. This chapter follows [the one dealing with the spies] in order to console the children by informing them that they would enter the land, for Bnei Yisrael grew weak and mourned. However, the real reason that this chapter follows the one dealing with the spies, is because all the congregation shouted and sinned. Hashem forgave their sin because of the prayer of Moshe. Scripture says, And when ye shall err (15:22). And they shall be forgiven (15:25) is proof of this. Scripture found it necessary to mention the law of the meal offering and of all burnt offerings and sacrifices. At the end, it states, But the soul that doeth aught with a high hand (v. 30). The latter alludes to Yisrael’s deeds. Scripture mentions the gatherer of wood (verses 32-34) because he acted with a high hand. Hashem designated the fringes as a sign because of His great pity on Yisrael, so that a person will not act with a high hand or forget.

Clearly uttered. Le-fale (clearly uttered) means to separate. Similarly the word ve-hiflah (shall make a division) in And Hashem shall make a division (Shemot 9:4). This is so even though ve-hiflah is spelled with a heh, for the letters alef, heh, vav, yod interchange.9.
A meal-offering of…fine flour. A tenth of an ephah for each one of the flock.

The he-lambs. Or the kids. Scripture similarly states later, for each lamb. If the celebrant offers a ram, then his meal offering is doubled, for a lamb is a small animal. Scripture does not mention the free-will offering along with the bullock. It mentions the peace offering [with the bullock] because it did not mention it above. They all have one law.
[According to the number.] The reference is to the meal offering, the oil, and the wine.
Or whosoever may be among you. Today.

As for the congregation. Some say that the heh prefixed to the word kahal (congregation) is the sign of the vocative. However, I believe that there is no vocative letter in the holy tongue. The four instances are proof of this. One of them is Moshe, Moshe. On the contrary, this heh is the sign of the definite object. It is not a sign of the vocative.
As ye are, so shall the stranger be. I have already explained the rule governing two kafs joined together.

[One law.] Its meaning is, one law aside from the burnt offerings, for the burnt offerings are obligated by statute. Hashem also says, as you bring a meal offering of fine flour along with the burnt offering, thus shall you do with your dough. There is no need to mention what our ancients, of blessed memory, received by tradition, namely, that one is obligated to set aside two offerings, a portion of the dough and a portion of the grain, and their amount. Their words are true. Everything else is nonsense.

[One he-goat.] Scripture adds a he-goat. The congregation must bring a sin offering whether they erred by doing something they were prohibited from doing or erred in not doing something they were obligated to do.

And their sin-offering. The reference is to the he-goat. A sei’r izzim (he-goat) refers to a young goat because the word se’ir (he-goat) is connected to izzim (goats). The reverse is the case with the term atud (he-goat).

A she-goat of the first year for a sin-offering. This explains a goat, a female (Vayikra 4:28). The sin spoken of in our verse refers to a failure, due to error, to do what the Torah commands. Now this law is the same for the one who errs and does what he is commanded not to do.
One law. This is similar to This is the law of (torat) the sin-offering (Vayikra 6:18).
With a high hand. To show all that he does not fear Hashem.
Blasphemeth. This is the way people speak.
Because he hath despised the word of Hashem. This is what with a high hand refers to.
And hath broken his commandment. For God commanded him not to act with a high hand. Others say that and hath broken His commandment refers to one who violates God’s commandment in secret.
That soul. This does not refer to the rational soul. as those who err say. It refers rather to the connection of the soul to the body.
His iniquity shall be upon him. Compare, his blood shall be upon him (Yechezkel 33:4).

In the wilderness. I believe that the reference is to the wilderness of Sinai. I have already mentioned why this chapter follows the incident of the spies. It is also possible that the gatherer of wood acted with a high hand and they warned him, but to no avail.[33. BROUGHT HIM.] Some say they brought him in on Saturday night.
In ward. Ba-mishmar (in ward) is vocalized with a pattach. It refers to a specific place.
What should be done to him. How he should be put to death.
As Hashem commanded. Death by stoning.

That they make them…fringes. It is possible to interpret this in two ways. One, that they make fringes (tzitzit) like those in by the fringes (be-tzitzit) of my head (Yechezkel 8:3), the reference in our verse being to threads that are not woven.
In the corners of their garments. Upon smooth garments or pants, for if pants are divided they will have corners.
A thread of blue. Upon the fringes. The reason the thread was blue is that blue is a sky-like color.

And it shall be unto you for a fringe. The thread at the end was like the fringe. The other interpretation is the one which the rabbis of blessed memory transmitted. Now the first interpretation is nullified in view of the fact that there are true witnesses to the second explanation. The rabbis transmitted to us the law that this commandment applies to a garment that has four corners and that the tzitzit are fringes. I will explain this law later. Now this commandment states that everyone who has a four-cornered garment shall always cover himself with it during the day. He shall not remove it so that he remembers the commandments. Those who pray with a tallit during the time of prayers do so because they read in the shema, And it shall be unto you for a fringe (v. 39) and that they make them throughout their generations fringes (v. 38). However, I believe that one is more obligated to enwrap oneself in fringes when he is not at prayer than during the time of prayer, so that he remembers the commandments and does not err and trespass during the other hours of the day, for in the hour of prayer he will not sin.
That ye may look upon it. The commandment requires that the fringes be seen.

After your own heart. Which lusts. The eye sees and the heart desires. The fringes thus serve as a sign and a mark that a person should not pursue the thoughts of his heart and all that his eyes desire.
After which ye use to go astray. For one who follows his desires goes astray from the service of his Elokim.

That ye may remember. Scripture has previously stated, and remember all the commandments of Hashem (v. 39). The meaning of our verse is: if you remember the commandments of Hashem, you will be holy and you will not defile yourselves with the lusts of the heart which defile the rational soul.
I am Hashem your Elokim. I am He who took you out of Mitzrayim to be your Elokim. I therefore say to you: I am Hashem your Elokim.

Now Korach, the son of izhar…took. This event occurred in the wilderness of Sinai when the first-born were set aside and the Leviyim were placed in their stead. Yisrael thought that our master Moshe acted out of his own will in giving his brother an elevated position. They suspected that he acted similarly towards the sons of Kehat, who were his relatives, and to all the sons of Levi who were of his family. The Leviyim rebelled against Moshe because they were subservient to Aharon and his sons. Datan and Aviram rebelled because Moshe removed the birthright from Reuven their forefather, and gave it to Yosef. It is also possible that they suspected that Moshe favored the tribe of Yosef because Yehoshua was his assistant. Korach too was a first-born, as Scripture clearly states. The banner of Reuven camped in the south. So did Korach, for he was a Kehati. The princes of the congregation were first-born. They offered the burnt offering. They therefore took the fire pans. The miracle of the staff, which demonstrated to all of Yisrael that Hashem chose the Leviyim in place of the first-born, is proof that this explanation is correct. Hence Scripture reads, that there may be made an end of their murmurings against Me (Bamidbar 17:25), for the murmuring was an account of this. Moshe also said, that I have not done them of mine own mind (v. 28). He said the aforementioned because Yisrael had come to believe that he had acted on his own. Furthermore, Moshe said, then Hashem hath not sent me (v. 29) in this thing, because Yisrael had come to believe in him. Here is another rigorous proof: seeing all the congregation are holy (v. 3). The aforementioned alludes to the first-born who are holy, for Scripture states, Sanctify unto Me all the first-born (Shemot 13:2). The first-born were the priests that come near to Hashem (Shemot 19:22). They were the most important ones of the congregation.

Now Korach…took. This is short for, now Korach took men. Compare, an ass bread (Shmuel I 16:20). There are many such instances in Scripture. Rabbi Yonah says that the meaning of Now Korach took is now Korach took himself to rise against Moshe.
In the face of Moshe. They did not rise up in secret. There is a difference between li-fene (in the face of) and mi-pene (before the face of) (Bereshit 3:8).
The elect men of the assembly. They were called to the tent of meeting.

Men of renown. Before they left Mitzrayim.A grammarian says that the princes of the congregation are the leaders who stood over those that were numbered (Bamidbar 1:4). He says that they are the object of took. Our text should be read as if written, And Korach and Datan and Aviram and On took the princes of Yisrael to speak to them. This interpretation is a bit far-fetched.
Ye take too much upon you. Enough for you. Its meaning is, you have grabbed the greater portion.
Seeing all the congregation are holy. For the entire congregation became holy from the day they stood on Sinai.

And Hashem is among them. For the Leviyim were chosen after Hashem’s glory dwelt amidst the children of Yisrael. Now if Moshe knew when he was on Mount Sinai that the tribe of Levi was chosen, Yisrael did not know.
Wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the assembly of the Lord? For Aharon to be kohen gadol (high priest) and Moshe, who taught Aharon, to be above him.
He fell upon his face. Willingly. Other say, like prophets when they receive a prophecy.
Who are his. Which is the chosen tribe. This was Moshe’s answer to Datan and Aviram and to the leaders of the congregation who were first-born.
And who is holy. In his tribe to be kohen gadol.
This. Test.

Ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi. The meaning of our clause is found in the following words of Moshe: Is it but a small thing unto you (v. 9). Scripture says, And Moshe said unto Korach (v. 8), for the first statement was addressed to Korach and to all of his company. However, this one was addressed to the Leviyim.
Is it but a small thing unto you. This means is it but a small thing unto you.
Before the congregation to minister unto them. When they bring their burnt offerings and sacrifices.
And that he hath brought thee near. And when he has brought you and your brothers near, will you seek the priesthood also?

Therefore. Therefore you and your whole congregation that art gathered together, rebel against Hashem. Its meaning is similar to And the rulers take counsel together, Against Hashem, and against His anointed (Tehillim 2:2). They gathered in order to fight with Hashem. When they strove against Hashem (Bamidbar 26:9) is similar. Some say that the heh prefixed to no’adim (gathered together) is superfluous.
And as to Aharon, what is he. What is his sin, what did he do?

We will not come up. It is possible that the tent of meeting was on a high place in the middle of the camp. Scripture therefore says, Get you up from about (v. 24). On the other hand, one who goes to serve Hashem or to the chosen place is said to go up.

Is it a small thing. Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey? Scripture reads, brought us up, because Mitzrayim is south of the Land of Yisrael, and one who comes from Mitzrayim to the land of Kenaan is in truth going up.
But thou must needs make thyself also a prince over us. You brought us out of Mitzrayim in order to make yourself a prince over us.
Must needs make thyself a prince over us. You and your brother also seek additional positions of power over us.

Moreover thou hast not brought us unto a land flowing with milk and honey. Its meaning is: You brought us out of a good place. Now if you had brought us to a place which is as good as the place you took us out of, and if you had given us fields and vineyards such as we had in Mitzrayim, and you sought power over us, then we would tolerate it. However, you removed us from a good place, from our fields and vineyards, and you did not bring us to a place as good as the one that you brought us out of. Why then do you seek power?

Wilt thou put out the eyes of these men? Its meaning is: you want to put out the eyes of these men. This alludes to those who left Mitzrayim. It is as if Korach said, you want to put out their eyes so that they do not see. But what you did is visible to the eyes. Therefore we will not come up. It is metaphoric to say so and so’s eyes are closed and he therefore cannot see. Others say its meaning is: Do you want to darken the eyes so that they do not see? In other words, you are fooling us. We will not come up. Others say its meaning is: even if you put out our eyes we will not go up. Korach said of these men because he spoke in the manner of the unintelligent, who do not want to say anything negative about themselves. However, I believe that of these men alludes to the elders who were with Moshe, for Scripture clearly states, and the elders of Yisrael followed him (v. 25).

And Moshe was very wroth. With what Korach said.I have already explained that the burnt offering and the meal offering put off the punishment of the wicked. Datan and Aviram were important men and offered meal offerings before this event. This is the meaning of Respect not their offering and turn to me, for I have not placed a burden upon one ass of their asses.
[I have not taken one ass from them.] I have not placed a burden upon one of their asses.
Neither have I hurt one of them. In any way.
And Moshe said unto Korach. Moshe had already said so. Thus this means: when Moshe said to Korach be before Hashem, they took their fire-pan.
Tomorrow. This occurred on the day that Moshe called to Datan and Aviram. It is possible that he called them earlier. The latter appears correct because Scripture reads, in the morning (v. 5).
With Moshe and Aharon. Moshe and Aharon with them.
Separate yourselves. For they were with them in front of the entrance to the tent of meeting.
And they fell upon their faces. To pray.

[O Elokim.] The term El (Elokim) indicates that Elokim has the power to destroy them in a moment. Elokim is the Elokim of the spirits. This explains the term El, for Elokim can destroy them because their spirits are in His hand.

Shall one man sin. The reference is to Korach, who assembled all of the congregation against Moshe and Aharon. There are those who say that the meaning of O Elokim, the Elokim of the spirits is: Elokim has the power to investigate human souls, for He is their Elokim. Elokim knows that one man, namely, Korach alone, sinned. He also knows if he [Korach] caused the others to sin.I believe that Separate yourselves from among this congregation refers to Korach and his congregation. A fire went out and devoured and destroyed them in one moment.

The dwelling of Korach. I believe that Korach had a tent for his household and his wealth. This tent was far from the camp of the Leviyim. The tents of Datan and Aviram were close to Korach’s tent, for only Leviyim camped around the tabernacle. We learn from this verse that the bearer of the banner camped close to the camp of the Leviyim.
And the elders of Yisrael followed him. I believe that the reference is to the chosen seventy elders.
And touch nothing of theirs. For if one comes to save their money they will go down to the pit like them.
In all their sins. Because of all their sins.
And their sons. The reference is to adults.
And their little ones. Male and female minors.

To do all these works. To have the Leviyim take the place of the first-born. Note, it is a major and grievous act to the one who does not believe that God ordered the first-born to be removed from their position as kohanim and to have this status conferred only upon the family of Moshe. All of this was done because of the incident of the golden calf, because and offered burnt-offerings, and brought peace-offerings (Shemot 32:6) speaks of the first-born who offered these sacrifices, for they alone were the kohanim. Also, the sons of Levi killed those who served the calf. There is a question here. Its answer is found in the Torah portion which opens with the words va-yelekh mosheh (Devarim 31:1).

But if the Lord make a new thing. Some say that the word beri’ah (a new thing) refers to the bringing forth of something that was never in existence.I have already explained that the word beri’ah is related to the word u-vara (hack) in and hack them (Yechezkel 23:47). Many cities have been split open, and those who dwelt in them have gone down to the pit. The meaning of bara is to cut.

And the ground open her mouth. The word u-fatzetah means and opened. Compare, yiftzeh (doth open) in doth open his mouth (Iyov 35:16).I have already hinted that man’s highest soul, which comes from the intermediary world, employs human language when speaking of things above her, for the body is its palace. It similarly employs human language when speaking of things below her. It does so in order that people understand her.
And their households. This is a general term for their wives, [grown] children, and their little ones.
And their goods. Which all of them possessed.
So they…went down. Its meaning is: when they went down, the earth closed and they were not seen.
And the earth closed upon them. The earth itself.
And they perished. For their children who were to take their place died.
At the cry of them. Because of their cry.

[And fifty men.] The heh of ha-chamishim (the fifty) is to be read as if written twice. Some say that Korach was among the ones who were swallowed. They offer as proof, And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korach (Bamidbar 26:10). Others say that Korach was burned. They offer, with Korach, when that company died; what time the fire devoured (Ibid.) as proof. Our sages say that Korach was burned and swallowed.I believe that only the place of Datan and Aviram split open, for no other place is mentioned. Korach was standing with his fire-pan with Aharon and the leaders of the congregation who were offering incense. With Korach (Bamidbar 26:10) is not connected to and swallowed them up (Ibid.) but rather to when that company died (Ibid.). This is the way the aforementioned verse is to be interpreted. If someone should argue and say, “Why isn’t Korach mentioned among those who were burned?” the answer is: once Scripture mentions that Korach’s company, which came to his aid, was burned, it is not necessary to mention Korach. For we know this by arguing from a minor to a major premise. Paroh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea (Shemot 15:4) is similar. Moshe does not mention in the song that Paroh drowned. The truth is that Paroh drowned, for Scripture explicitly states, But overthrew Paroh and his host in the Red Sea (Tehillim 136:15). The verse that he fare not as Korach, and as his company (Bamidbar 17:5) is proof that Korach was among those who were burned.
And scatter thou the fire yonder. From the altar.
For they are become holy. The fire-pans are holy because they [Korach and his company] offered them before the Lord.
Even the fire-pans of these men who have sinned. This explains the fire-pans (v. 2).
And let them be made. The reference is to the workers.
Beaten plates. Compare, And they did beat (ve-yerakke’u) the gold into thin plates (Shemot 39:3).
[For they are become holy.] Because they were offered before Hashem explains for they are become holy.
That they may be a sign. A memorial and a mark.
And they beat them out. The beaters beat them out.
As Hashem spoke unto him by the hand of Moshe. Unto him (lo) refers to Aharon. Others say that unto him refers to Korach. However, I believe the latter to be farfetched.
On the morrow. Of this day, for mochorat (morrow) is always connected to the previous day.

Ye have killed. Its meaning is, what proof is this that the tribe of Levi is the chosen one, and that Aharon was chosen to be kohen gadol? It is possible that those who offered the fire-pans were burned because of your prayer or through your knowledge of the sciences.
When the congregation was assembled. Whenever the word kehillah (assembly) is followed by the word al (on), it refers to an assembly for the sake of quarreling.
And Moshe and Aharon came. Because they saw that God’s glory appeared.
Get you up. For they sat in the tabernacle, which was on the high ground in the camp of the Leviyim, as I explained in my comments on Get you up (Bamidbar 16:24).
And they fell upon their faces. To pray.
Take thy fire-pan. The reference is to a specific fire-pan.
And lay incense thereon. Scripture does not say, and lay “the” incense on. The intelligent will understand.

And carry. The word holekh (and carry) is an imperative. It is similar to the word hoshev (make to dwell) in make thy father…to dwell (Bereshit 47:6). Holekh comes from the same root as helikhi (take away) (Shemot 2:9). It means bring, the idea being it should go with you.

[And Aharon returned.] And Aharon returned is connected to the section that follows, even though it is separated. I have already given you many such examples. When Aharon returned and the plague was stayed, Hashem spoke.

Rods. Some say that the rod of Levi is not Elokim’s rod, for Elokim’s rod was already known. Why then write Aharon’s name on it. Others say that the rod was like the other rods. There was no difference between them. This interpretation appears correct to me.
[One for each father’s house.] Each father’s house means each tribe. Reuven and Shimon are examples.
[For there shall be one rod.] Scripture tells us that there shall be one rod for the tribe of Levi because this tribe was divided into kohanim and Leviyim.
Where I meet with you. Permanently.

I will make to cease. The word ve-hashikkoti (I will make to cease) comes from a double root. It is similar to the word ve-hatimmoti (and I will consume) in and I will consume thy filthiness from out of thee (Yechezkel 22:15). It is related to the word shakhakhah (assuaged) in then was the king’s wrath assuaged (Esther 7:10).Ve-hashikkoti (I will make to cease) means I [God] will find rest. Scripture employs human language. The rod of Levi was among the twelve. Behold, the tribe of Yosef was represented by one rod.
For the house of Levi. The word matteh (rod of) is to be read as if written twice. Our verse is to be read as if written: the rod of Aharon, the rod of the house of Levi.

And bore ripe almonds. The word va-yigmol (and bore ripe) is related to the word va-yigammal (and was weaned) in And the child grew, and was weaned (Bereshit 21:8). Many say that the rod came from an almond tree because the rod bore almonds. However, this is not proof. The word shekedim (almonds) has midrashically been related to the word shoked (watch) in I watch over My word to perform it (Yirmiyahu 1:12).
And they looked. At the handwriting of each one.

And the children of Yisrael spoke unto Moshe, saying. It is enough for us that we perished and were undone. Now, in addition, everyone that comes near the tabernacle will die like those who were burnt. O that we should cease dying. Hashem then spoke to Aharon, who was the leader of the tribe of Levi, and cautioned him that the Leviyim not cause Bnei Yisrael to stumble. The meaning of unto Aharon (Bamidbar 18:1) is that Hashem communicated with Aharon through Moshe. On the other hand, the clause may be taken at face value, because Aharon too was a prophet. Also, this section is proof that the rebellion took place in the desert of Sinai when the tabernacle was erected and the Leviyim were chosen, and the first-born were disqualified.
The iniquity of the Sanctuary. Which is on the inside of the veil. Its meaning is, if you do not guard the sanctuary the sin is upon you.
[And thy fathers’ house.] For they carried the sanctuary.
The iniquity of your priesthood. If you do not keep the laws of the priesthood, the sin is upon you.

The tribe of thy father. The reference is to Levi. Our sages say that the tribe of thy father is to be taken at face value. However, I believe that it is to be explained in keeping with my earlier interpretation. Our verse is to be read as if written, the tribe of Levi which is the tribe of your father.

That they may be joined. The meaning of ve-yillavu is similar to ve-nispechu (and they shall join) (Is. 14:1). So too the word yillaveh (be joined) in Now this time will my husband be joined (Bereshit 29:34). Look, the Leviyim are joined by their names.
Thou and thy sons with thee. You and your sons, and not the Leviyim, shall abide before the tent of meeting.
Neither they, nor ye. It is the way of Scripture to speak in this manner. Compare, Rule thou over us, also you, also thy son (Jud. 8:22). That means this one is like this one.
[And they shall be joined unto thee.] So that you do not need the services of a stranger, namely, a Yisraeli.

As a service of gift. And someone who is a common man in regard to the priesthood even if he be a Levi [shall be put to death]. The burnt offering of Shmuel, who was a Levi, is no argument for it was a temporary ruling, as was the case of Gidon.
For a consecrated portion. I have already explained this.
Of the most holy things. For there are offerings that have a lesser degree of sacredness.
Reserved from the fire. Of all that they sanctify, for isheh (fire-offering) and esh (fire) mean the same, the heh of isheh being superfluous.

And every meal-offering of theirs. After they sanctify the memorial part thereof. [AND EVERY SIN-OFFERING OF THEIRS, AND EVERY GUILT-OFFERING OF THEIRS.] After they offer the designated organs of the sin offering and the guilt offering. WHICH THEY MAY RENDER
Unto me. The reference is to a trespass. Now the meal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering are holier than the peace offerings.

In a most holy place shalt thou eat thereof. Even in a most holy place, namely, in the tent of meeting shalt thou eat thereof. The tent of meeting is called a most holy place in contrast to the courtyard of the tabernacle.

Their gift. A tav is missing in the word mattanam (their gift). Mattanam is similar to the word pinnah (corner), which has the meaning of pinnatah (her corner) in Passing through the street near her corner (Mishlei 7:8). On the other hand, we may be dealing with two forms.

All the best of the oil. Chelev (the best) means the most precious, the best. The reference is to the cream of the oil, for the word yitzhar (oil) means light. Its root is tzadi, heh, resh. The reference is to the fat of the olive oil.
The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their land. The first of all the fruits of the ground.

[Every one that is clean in thy house may eat thereof.] This verse warns that only the clean in your house may eat of fat things and of the breast of waving and the thigh of heaving and also everything dedicated by a Yisraeli. The Yisraeli shall not eat of the latter, for it belongs to God. You [the kohen] may eat of it.
Shalt thou surely redeem. You shall accept the redemption money of the first-born. You shall similarly accept the redemption of the first-born of the unclean beast.
And their redemption-money. This only refers to the first-born of humans.

Thou shalt not redeem. For they are holy. You shall not accept their redemption money. Many say that the word redeem refers to Bnei Yisrael. However, the reverse is true for the word tokhelunu (thou shalt eat it) (Devarim 15:20), in which the prefix thou refers to the kohen, for Thou shalt eat it refers to the one who is obligated to eat it.

Covenant of salt. A “cut covenant.” The word melach (salt) is related to the word melechah (salt) in A fruitful land turned into salt (Tehillim 107:34). A salted place is said to be cut off, for nothing grows there. Compare, brimstone, and salt (Devarim 29:22).
In return. The word chelef means in return.
And henceforth…shall not come nigh. This was written because of Korach’s assembly.
But the Leviyim alone shall do the service. The word hu means himself. Others say that hu is the object. However, this is incorrect, for the service of the tent of meeting is the object.
And they shall bear their iniquity. If they do not keep the charge. Now, the tithe is their inheritance. I therefore stated: [and among the children of Yisrael they shall have no inheritance].
And Hashem spoke unto Moshe, saying. To Moshe, not to Aharon, for Scripture goes on to say that the Leviyim are to give a tithe to Aharon from the tithe [they received].
And as the fulness. I have already explained the meaning of the word mele’ah (fullness).
Of all the best thereof. The meaning of mi-kol chelbo is, of all the best thereof. And ye shall eat the fat (chelev) of the land (Bereshit 45:18) is similar.
Even the hallowed part thereof. For the tenth part thereof is the holy part.

[When ye set apart the best thereof.] This has already been mentioned by Scripture. It is repeated in order to connect it to that which follows. Its meaning is, you are prohibited to eat of it until you set apart the best thereof, and afterwards it shall be counted [as the grain of the threshing floor] and you may eat it in every clean place.

And ye shall bear no sin by reason of it. This means when you set apart the best of it you shall bear no sin through it. Furthermore, when you give the hallowed part thereof, the sacred donations of the children of Yisrael will be preserved. However, if you do not offer to tithe, then you will bear a sin, for you will have trespassed the commandment and profaned the holy things of the children of Yisrael because you ate its holy part.

This is the statute. This chapter was also stated at Sinai. It was given when Hashem commanded that they put out of the camp…whosoever is unclean by the dead (Bamidbar 5:2). There were also people who were unclean by coming into contact with a dead body when Passover arrived (Bamidbar 9:6). This chapter is placed here because it relates to the kohen.

A Red Heifer, faultless. The heifer is not to be small. The Gaon says that the water of sprinkling (v. 13) is similar to honey, which is injurious to the one who has red bile but stimulates the one who has phlegm. However, there is no need for this interpretation.

And she shall be brought forth. Someone shall bring her forth. Or it means he shall have her brought forth by his command. The same applies to ve-shachat (and she shall be slain), for Elazar did not slaughter the heifer. The word le-fanav (before his face) proves the latter.

And the heifer shall be burnt in his sight. Ve-saraf et ha-parah (and the heifer shall be burnt) is to be rendered, and someone shall burn the heifer. The term le’enav (in his sight) proves the latter interpretation.
Cedar-wood. As in the case of a leper. I have hinted there at some secret.
Then the priest shall wash his clothes. The kohen who burns it.

And the priest shall be unclean. The meaning of ve-tame ha-kohen (and the priest shall be unclean) is, and the kohen has already been unclean, or, as some say, the kohen shall be unclean. Until the even refers to the eating of sacred food.
A man that is clean. The reference is not to the kohen who burns the cow.
A water of sprinkling. The meaning of niddah (sprinkling) is distance. Compare, me-naddekhem (that hate you) (Is. 66:5).
And be unclean until the even. Once Scripture states that the gatherer of the ashes shall wash his clothes there is no need to mention that he shall wash in water.
And unto the stranger that sojourneth among them. For the Land of Yisrael is holy because God’s glory is there.
Even any man’s dead body. Be it the body of a Yehudi or a non-Jew.
Man’s…body. Not the body of an animal.
Shall be unclean. The meaning of ve-tame is, shall be unclean. It is a future form, for the vav changes the verb from a perfect to an imperfect. However, I believe that ve-tame is in the past tense.

The same shall purify himself therewith. The meaning of hu yitchate vo (the same shall purify himself therewith) is, he shall remove his sin therewith. On the other hand, the word yitchate (shall purify himself) is similar to the word techatteni (purge me) in Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean (Tehillim 51:9). Those who are acquainted with the secret of numbers know that the number three is like the number seven.

Because the water of sprinkling. Some say that that me niddah (the water of sprinkling) has the same meaning as me niddah (water of sprinkling) in it shall be purified with the water of sprinkling (Bamidbar 31:23).
Was not dashed. The word zorak (dashed) refers to the water.
Is yet. The word od (is yet) means continuously. Compare, od (while) in While the earth remaineth (Bereshit 8:22).
In a tent. A house has the same law as a tent. Scripture mentions a tent because Yisrael then lived in tents. That killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp (Vayikra 17:3) is similar.
And every thing that is in the tent. Garments.
Covering close-bound. Two coverings.
Or a grave. Of a human being.
And for the unclean they shall take. See, Scripture explains how one who comes into contact with the dead shall purge himself.
A clean person. The reference is most probably to a kohen.

But the man that shall be unclean. Scripture has already mentioned, Whosoever toucheth the dead…that soul shall be cut off from Yisrael (v. 13). It now warns the one who touches a bone or a grave [not to defile the sanctuary].
Shall be unclean until even. And shall not become clean until he washes.
And whatsoever the unclean person toucheth shall be unclean. The reference is to one who has become unclean by touching a dead body, a bone, or a grave.
Shall be unclean until even. And washes.
In the first month. In the fortieth year. Look, the Torah does not contain any act or prophecy except in the first and the fortieth year.

[And the children of Yisrael, even the whole congregation, came.] Scripture states this because the generation that left Mitzrayim died in the wilderness and they who were entering Kenaan came to the desert of Tzin.
And the people abode in Kadesh. For they dwelt there for many days. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.

And there was no water for the congregation. Scripture tells of two incidents. One, the death of Miriam. Two, the death of Aharon and Moshe and their failure to enter the land. It begins by telling the cause of the latter.
And the people strove. Va-yarev (strove) is a hifil.
When our brethren perished. Bi-geva (when…perished) is an infinitive. It is similar to ki-shekav (when…shall sleep) in when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers (Melachim I 1:21).
Our brethren. The generation that died in the desert. They were servants of Hashem.
And why have ye brought. This was addressed to Moshe and Aharon, for Scripture goes on to say, and they assembled themselves together against Moshe and against Aharon (v. 2).
Scripture reads, And the people strove with Moshe, (v. 3) because their quarrel with Moshe was more intense.
Have ye made us to come up. He’elitunu (have ye made us to come up) is irregular.
And Moshe and Aharon went from the presence of the assembly. Like those who flee.
And fell upon their faces. To pray. Other interpret, to prophetically inquire of Hashem.

Take the rod. Many interpretations are offered for this incident. There is an individual opinion that Moshe sinned because he said to Yisrael, who are the children of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov: Hear now, ye rebels (v. 10). However, if this were the case why did he again say, ye have been rebellious against Hashem (Devarim 9:7). Others say that the word ve-dibbartem (and speak ye) has the meaning, and ye shall strike. It is similar to the word va-tedabber (and destroyed) in and destroyed all the seed royal (Divrei Hayamim II 22:10). However, this is incorrect, for va-tedabber is related to the word dever (destruction) or to the word yadber (he subdueth) in He subdueth peoples under us (Tehillim 47:4). Va-tedabber thus means, and destroyed. Indeed, it so reads in the other book. The meaning of ve-dibbartem el ha-sela (and speak ye unto the rock) thus is, and ye shall destroy the rock. Furthermore, if this is the meaning of the word, why was Moshe punished? The above commentaries answer, because he hit the rock twice. However, if this is the case why was Aharon punished? Rabbi Moshe Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that some signs are performed by word of mouth, others by action and speech, as in the case of the salt which Elisha cast into the water. Hashem commanded Moshe to take the staff and strike the rock as he did in the case of the rock [at Chorev]. He added the word ve-dibbartem (and speak ye) so that the water would flow via the speech and the blow. Because Yisrael angered him, Moshe said, are we to bring you forth water from the rock? What Moshe meant was, we do not have the power to bring water out of the rock. We can only do so by the power of Hashem. Now Moshe did not make himself clear. People thought what he said was that Hashem cannot bring water out of the rock. This is the meaning of because ye sanctified Me not in the midst of the children of Yisrael (Devarim 32:51). Rabbi Moshe offered proof from the words of the poet who said, For they embittered his spirit, And he spoke rashly with his lip (Tehillim 106:33). The sin was thus in his expressing, not by striking [the rock]. However, this too is incorrect, for Moshe said, are we to bring you forth water out of this rock (v. 10). Why was Aharon punished? Furthermore, no speech is mentioned in the Torah’s description of the act of striking the rock. The proof offered by Rabbi Moshe is no proof because the meaning of For they embittered his spirit is that they embittered Hashem’s spirit. Scripture similarly writes, But they rebelled, and grieved His holy spirit (Is. 63:10). This is the meaning of They angered Him also at the waters of Merivah (Tehillim 106:32). It means they angered Hashem. Scripture similarly states, These are the waters of Merivah, where the children of Yisrael strove with Hashem (Bamidbar 20:13). Scripture says, And it went ill with Moshe because of them (Tehillim 106:32) because they embittered Hashem’s spirit, and He decreed that Moshe not enter the land. Others say that the meaning of speak to the rock can only mean strike the rock, for a rock cannot hear. Now if this is so, why was Moshe punished? Some say that Moshe and Aharon were punished because they did not sing a song of praise as in Spring up, O well-sing ye unto it (Bamidbar 21:17). They say that this is the meaning of because ye sanctified Me not (Devarim 32:51). Others say that Hashem commanded Moshe and Aharon to speak to the rock, but they did not speak to it. On the contrary, Moshe struck the rock. Therefore they were both punished and they were told, ye trespassed (Devarim 32:51); ye rebelled (v. 24); ye believed not in Me (v. 12), and ye sanctified Me not (Devarim 32:52). Those who are guided by reason say that it is impossible that a messenger of Hashem would alter Hashem’s word. If Moshe transformed Hashem’s word, how can we believe his Torah? However, the aforementioned also spoke incorrectly, for if Moshe had altered a commandment he would have been punished immediately. Look, Moshe was punished with regard to something which was not an eternal commandment and not a law given to Yisrael. Nor did he knowingly violate Hashem’s command. He only did so inadvertently because Yisrael angered him. Moshe clearly said, Also Hashem was angry with me for your sakes (Devarim 1:37). Others say that Yisrael told Moshe to bring water out of a different rock. They offer this rock as proof (v. 10). However, Moshe was afraid to alter Hashem’s word. Moshe was punished because he did not believe that he would be able to bring forth water from the rock that Yisrael chose. He was therefore punished. This is the meaning of ye believed not in Me (v. 12). This interpretation is also incorrect, for Scripture states, ye rebelled against My word (v. 24). However, they did not rebel.I will reveal in hints the explanation which appears correct to me. Know, when the part knows the All, he cleaves to the All and creates signs and wonders with the help of the All. Now it is true that Hashem told Moshe and Aharon, speak ye unto the rock. They did not speak to the rock because the people were quarreling with Moshe. The “part” thus remained a “part.” He struck the rock, and water did not come out of it until he struck it a second time. Moshe and Aharon thus did not sanctify Hashem’s name. They inadvertently rebelled and trespassed. It is also possible to explain that And he spoke rashly with his lips (Tehillim 106:33) refers to Moshe. It was unseemly for Moshe to say anything before fulfilling Hashem’s command. Moshe was therefore punished. The midrashic interpretation of our ancients, of blessed memory, who said that Moshe sinned because he said, Hear now, ye rebels (v. 10) is also in keeping with this interpretation. The rabbis hint at this secret.
Unto the rock. Which I pointed out to you or which is found close to the camp.

That it give forth its water. Many erred and said that the rock is to be identified with the stone [at Chorev] because Scripture reads, its water. However, they cannot think straight. The stone was in Chorev and this rock was at the border of the land of Edom, for it was in Kadesh. It is also possible to interpret its water as meaning, the water which I will place in it.
The rod from before Hashem. The reference is to the rod of Elokim. It was the rod which was placed before the testimony.
Are we to bring you forth water out of this rock? Do we have the power to bring forth water out of this rock for you?
Because ye believed not in me. This alludes to the secret at which I hinted, i.e., that Hashem’s name was not sanctified through them.
And he was sanctified in them. Through Moshe and Aharon. Our verse has the same meaning as Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified (Vayikra 10:3).

From Kadesh. Kadesh is the name of a place where a city is located. It is not to be identified with Kadesh Barnea, for the latter was a wilderness. Thus Scripture reads, Hashem shaketh the wilderness of Kadesh (Tehillim 29:8).
The travail. I have already explained the meaning of the word tela’ah (travail).
Mitzrim dealt ill with us, and our fathers. Who died. The meaning of our clause is that their evil lasted a very long time.

And sent an angel. This is to be taken literally. Scripture similarly states, And the angel of His presence saved them (Is. 63:9). Many said that the reference is to Moshe for they found Then spoke Chaggai Hashem’s messenger (malakh) (Chaggai 1:13). However, this is not my opinion.
Through field or through vineyard. So that they do not destroy it. We will not even drink the water of your wells.
We will go along the king’s highway. The major highway upon which the king travels. Or its meaning is, the road that the king, namely, the king of Edom, will command us to travel in.
We will go up by the highway. What harm will it cause you if we up by the highway? If we need water you will sell it to us. This is the meaning of mikhram (v. 19). It means the price thereof.

[The children of Yisrael.] Its meaning is, the entire congregation. Because Edom went to fight against them, Scripture relates that no one was missing from the children of Yisrael when they came from the city of Edom to Mount Hor.
Aharon shall be gathered unto his people. This is similar to and die in the mount (Devarim 32:50). It means that Aharon should prepare himself to die, and go up the mountain.
Ye have rebelled. I have explained this.
At the waters of Merivah. Le-me merivah means at the waters of Merivah. It is the name of a place. Or le-me merivah means because of the waters of Merivah.
And strip…and put them upon. Ve-hafshet (and strip) and ve-hilbashtam (and put them upon) are hifils.
[And Aharon shall be gathered.] Its meaning is, as soon as you strip Aharon of his garments, he shall die.
And Aharon was gathered to his people. I have explained this.
And when all the congregation saw. When they saw the event which occurred, they wept for thirty days.
[Died.] I have already explained the meaning of the term.

And the Kenaani, the king of Arad. The ancients said he is Sichon. He is called a Kenaani, for all Emori are Kenaani. Many say that Yehoshua wrote this section. The king of Arad, one (Yehoshua 12:14) is proof of this. They also found that Scripture states that the children of Yehudah called the name of the place Chormah. However, they are wrong, for that place was originally called Tzfat while the place spoken of in our verse was ruled by the king of Arad. In reality they are two places. There are many such instances in Scripture. According to the plain meaning of the text the king of Arad ruled over the eastern bank of the Yarden. This portion was connected to the death of Aharon, because Scripture relates what happened on Mount Hor before they [Yisrael] journeyed from there. And the Kenaani, the king of Arad… heard…and they journeyed from mount Hor (v. 4) is proof of this. If you want to find what the king of Arad heard, observe, it is clearly stated.
That Yisrael came by the way of atharim. Some say that the alef of atharim is superfluous. They say that the meaning of ha-atharim is, those who spy. The alef of ezro’akha (your arm) is similar.
To compass the land of Edom. Tzalmonah and Punon, for this is explicitly stated in Scripture.
This light bread. The word ha-kelokel (this light) means the very light. The word is formed by doubling the word kal. There are many similar instances in Scripture.

And the Lord…serpents. The word ha-serafim (fiery) is an adjective. The following is a midrashic interpretation. Scripture states, If the serpent bite before it is charmed, Then the charmer hath no advantage (Kohelet 10:11). These people sent their tongues to bite. They were repaid with snakes being sent against them.
Make thee. A form of a fiery serpent out of brass, for Scripture explicitly says so.

And set it upon a pole. So that it be on a high place and everyone will be able to see it. Many err. They say that this was an image that had the capability of receiving powers from on high. Far be it, far be it [for one to believe such a thing], for this thing was made by Hashem’s command. We should not investigate why Moshe was commanded to make the form of a snake. Should someone disagree, let him show us if there is a tree that makes bitter waters sweet. Even honey will not sweeten them. What reason was there to put a cake of figs upon a boil? It is not in the nature of figs to remove boils. The truth is that the mind of the Almighty is beyond us.

And the children of Yisrael journeyed. From the land of Edom, for Scripture states, to compass the land of Edom (v. 4). Punon is on the far border of Edom. Bnei Yisrael traveled from Punon to Ovot, for Scripture says so.
And pitched in the valley of zered. Zared is elsewhere referred to as Divon Gad.
For Arnon is the border of Moav. It was so at first.

In the book of the wars of Hashem. It was a separate book in which the wars of Hashem on behalf of His servants was recorded. It is possible that it originated in the days of Avraham, for many books, such as the work of Natan and Ido, the chronicles of the kings of Yisrael, and the songs of Shlomo and his proverbs, were lost and are not found among us.

Vaheb in suphah. There were wars in these mentioned places in ancient times. The word Vaheb is not Hebrew. Neither is Vofsi (Bamidbar 13:14), Vashti (Esther 1:9), Vaizatha (Esther 9:9), and also Vashni (Divrei Hayamim I 6:13). It is possible that the vav of Vashni is a connective. I say all this because we do not find the vav to be a root letter at the beginning of a word except in the word vave (hooks) in the hooks of the pillars (Shemot 27:10). It is found only in place of a yod. Compare, valed (child) (Shmuel II 6:23). The explanation of the Aramaic translation is known.
And the slope of the valleys. Some say that the word eshed (slope) is Aramaic. The end of the matter is: all of these are names of places.
That inclineth. The reference is to Bnei Yisrael, for they passed by Ar.

And leaneth upon the border of Moav. This is what and they abide over against me (Bamidbar 22:5) refers to. Yisrael journeyed from there to a place called be’er, for the heh of be’erah (to Be'er) is in place of the word el (to). It is like the heh of mitzraymah (to Mitzrayim) (Bereshit 12 :10). This well was also the result of a miracle. I believe that it is not the well which is called Miriam’s well. On the contrary, it refers to a place that Moshe commanded to be dug. The princes of Yisrael dug it with their staffs, and water immediately gushed forth.
Spring up, o well. This is how the song opened. Scripture does not record the entire song.
Sing ye unto it. The word enu (sing) is an imperative. Note, Scripture explains how it came into being.
Which the nobles of the people delved. Scripture repeats itself, as is its style.

With the sceptre. The meaning of bi-mechokek (with the sceptre) is, by the governors. Compare, My heart is toward the governors (chokeke) of Yisrael (Jud. 5:9). This well was in the wilderness, far from an inhabited place. From this wilderness Yisrael journeyed to Matanah. From Matanah they journeyed to Nachaliel. Note that eshed ha-nehalim (the slope of the valleys) and the wilderness which is called Be'er and Matanah and Nachaliel are all names of places. They are also referred to by a general name, viz., Almon-diblathiam (Bamidbar 33:46), which is found in the Torah portion Ve-Elleh Mase (Ibid.). On the other hand, it is also possible that these are the names of places that Bnei Yisrael passed over in another journey. The mountains of Avarim in front of Nevo (Bamidbar 33:47) are to be identified with Bamot and the valley that is in the field of Moav (v. 20). The following is proof of this. Scripture states that Yisrael journeyed from the valley to the plains of Moav by the Yarden at Yericho (Bamidbar 22:1). It also states that Yisrael journeyed from the mountains of Avarim to the plains of Moav beyond the Jordon at Yericho (Bamidbar 33:48). It further states, So we abode in the valley over against Beit Peor (Devarim 3:29) at the time that I [Moshe] pleaded [with God]. Scripture elsewhere states, Get thee up into this mountain of Avarim, unto mount Nevo (Devarim 32:49). Scripture also states, and he was buried in the valley (Devarim 34:6). The Torah there states, And Moshe went up from the plains of Moav unto mount Nevo to the top of Pisgah (Devarim 34:1). The valley was thus at the top of Pisgah. Moshe died there, and there was no need to move him after his death.
Which looketh down. Ve-nishkafah (which looketh down) is in the feminine. It refers to the valley.

Upon the desert. The word yeshimon (desert) means a wasteland (shemamah). And in the waste, a howling wilderness (yeshimon) (Devarim 32:10) is the proof text. So too is They wandered in the wilderness (yeshimon) in a desert way (Tehillim 107:4).
To jahaz. Yahtzah means to Yahatz.
From the Arnon. Which he [the king of Edom] took from Moav.

Even unto the children of Amon. Scripture records that half of the land of Amon belonged to the children of Yisrael, for they took it from the Emori who originally took it from the children of Amon. Now Scripture tells us that Hashem would not give Bnei Yisrael even the size of a footstep from any of the land belonging to Bnei Amon and Moavim. The reference is to the land which Amon and Moav possessed at that time. Scripture therefore had to record the words of the poets. It did so because Yisrael lived in Cheshbon. The Torah explicitly states, And Yisrael dwelt in all the cities of the Emori, in Cheshbon (v. 25).
And in all the towns thereof. Cheshbon is like a mother, and the towns are like daughters.
For Cheshbon was the city of Sichon. It turned into the city of Sichon, for, as was well known, he fought against the former king of Moav.
They that speak in parables. Who invent parables on their own.
[Come ye to Cheshbon.] They said this to the Emori.
Be built. Better than before.
And established. To be the city of Sichon.
For a fire is gone out of Cheshbon. This alludes to the people of Cheshbon who conspired against their king.
A flame. The idea is repeated in accord with poetic style.
From the city of Sichon. From the city that today belongs to Sichon.
Ar of Moav. Ar is the name of a place. It is in Moav. Compare, Beth-lehem Yehudah (Rut 1:1).
The high places. Bamot means the high places.
Kmosh. The name of an idol; Moav’s god.
Fugitives. Those who flee. Fugitives that run from the sword.

We have shot them. These are the words of Moshe. The mem of va-niram (we shot at them) refers to the king of the Emori and his troops. It has two interpretations. One, that va-niram is related to the word nir (kingship). It is to be read as if written twice. It is like even the prophecy, Oded the prophet (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8). Our verse means, and their king the king of Cheshbon was destroyed. Va-niram is similar to the word ha-oholi (my tent) in in the midst of my tent (Yehoshua 7:21), and to ha-erkekha (thy valuation) (Vayikra 27:23). Va-niram avad cheshbon (we have shot at them—Cheshbon is perished) means, their king, that is, the king of Cheshbon, perished. Second, that va-niram is related to yereh va-yor (shoot; and he shot) (Melachim II 13:17) and yariti (cast) (Bereshit 31:51). It means, when we shot them Cheshbon was destroyed.

And we have laid waste. Va-nashim comes from a double root. The chirik is in place of a short kamatz. Compare, va-yasev (led about) in But Elokim led the people about (Shemot 13:18). Rabbi Moshe Ha-Kohen says that the dagesh in the shin of va-nashim compensates for a missing alef. Compare, Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth (Iyov. 35:11) wherein an alef is missing in the word mallefenu (teacheth us). The word va-nashim is related to the word tesham (shall bear her guilt) in Shomron shall bear her guilt (Hoshea 14:1). Some say that Cheshbon was always the city of Sichon. In this case, Come ye to Cheshbon (v. 27) is the line that the poets directed at the Moavim who came as captive to Cheshbon. And for a fire is gone out of Cheshbon is a metaphor for the army of Sichon. When the poets speak on behalf of the Moavim, they say, we thought that Cheshbon will be destroyed and the entire land will be laid waste even unto Nofach. Or these are the words of Moshe.
And they turned. I have already explained its meaning.
Edrei. To Edrei. Scripture is being brief.
None left him remaining. No one of Bnei Yisrael.

To the Emori. The lamed prefixed to the word emori (Emori) is vocalized with a kamatz. Its reference is to the famous Emori Sichon and Og. There were no kings among the Kenaani as great as they. Whose height was like the height of the cedars (Amos 2:9) is proof of this.
And Moav was sore afraid. Va-yagar means was afraid. Guru lakhem (be ye afraid) (Iyov 19:29) is similar.

And Moav was overcome with dread. Va-yakatz (overcome with dread) has the same meaning as a similarly spelled word whose letters are inverted. U-nekitzennah (and vex it) in Let us go up against Yehudah, and vex it (Is. 7:6) is similar.
Unto the elders of Midyan. It is possible that the five Midyani kings are these same elders.
Now will this multitude lick up…as the ox licketh up. Yelachakhu (will…lick up) and ki-lechokh (as…licketh up) are two different conjugations.
To pethor. Pethorah means to Petor. Compare, mitzrayemah (to Mitzrayim) (Bereshit 37:25).

To the land of the children of his people. Who were Aram. Scripture similarly states, from Petor of Aram Naharayim (Devarim 23:5). The midrash identifies Bilam with Bela. [However, the identification is untenable] because Bilam was an Arami. If we identify Bilam with Bela because of Beor his father, then, lo and behold, the son of Achashverosh lived before Achashverosh. They are definitely two different people.
Which is by the river. The reference is to Aram Naharayim.
The face of the earth. I have already explained the meaning of this expression.

Curse me. The word arah (curse) is an imperative. It comes from a double root with one of the double letters missing. The same is true of with the word kavah (curse) in curse me (v. 18). The word kov (curse) is vocalized according to the paradigm of shemor (keep). Kavah in kavah li (curse me) minus the heh follows the paradigm of shechav (lie), rekhav (ride), and tzelach (rested on).

That we may smite them. Nakkeh (that we may smite them) is an infinitive. The fact that it ends in a heh is no argument against the latter, for the word le-khalle (to finish), in to finish the transgression (Daniel 9:24) is similar.

Is cursed. The silent vav of yu’ar (is cursed) is in place of a dagesh, which is in place of the missing double letter. Compare, yusav (turned about) in turned about upon the cummin (Is. 28:27). There is no other word like it in this form, because of the rules concerning gutturals.
The elders of Moav. The wise men.

With the rewards of divination in their hand. Rabbi Shmuel Ha-Nagid the Sephardi, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of u-kesamim (with the reward of divination) is payment for divination. He offers as proof the word be-yadam (in their hand). However, he says nothing. U-kesamim be-yadam is to be taken literally. Scripture tells us that Balak sent diviners like himself to the diviner [Bilam]. Furthermore, Bilam would not be able to tarry, saying, “I can not find a propitious day, and a propitious hour to go and curse,” for the messengers were members of his guild. In his right hand is the instrument of divination (ha-kesom) (Ez. 21:27) is proof that u-kesamim be-yadam is to be taken literally.
And I will bring you back word. After you spend the night here.

And Elokim came. Out of regard for Yisrael, for Hashem knew the coming incident of ba’al pe’or. Now if Bilam had cursed them then, all of the world would have said that the plague came because of Bilam’s curse.

What men are these. This was a way of opening and starting a conversation. It is similar to Where is Hevel thy brother (Bereshit 4:9). Now Kayin denied [knowledge of Hevel’s whereabouts]. However, Hashem told him, the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth out unto Me (Bereshit 4 :10).
For they are blessed. Its meaning is, you cannot curse them, for I have blessed them.

The princes of Balak. Scripture does not mention the elders of Midyan, for Balak was the protagonist and he sent the messengers to Bilam. Rabbi Moshe Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that even though the yod is the sign of the object it can only come with a nun. Compare, ha-lehorgeni (thinkest thou to kill me) (Shemot 2:14). It does not read ha-lehorgi. However, he forgot le-titti (to give me) in to give me leave to go with you [our verse] and yabbemi (perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me) in he will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me (Devarim 25:7). Rabbi Yonah the grammarian says that the yod of le-titti is superfluous, but what he says is incorrect.
[To come with us.] Its meaning is, to go with us from his place.
